question: Explain the main derivative instruments a company can use to manage interest rate risk.
sources: Hull, J. C., Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives - interest rate forwards, futures, swaps and options
Reserve Bank of India directions on rupee interest rate derivatives

points.label: Forward rate agreement
points.description: An over-the-counter contract fixing the interest rate for a notional amount for a future period; only the difference between the agreed rate and the market rate is settled.

points.label: Interest rate futures
points.description: Standardised exchange-traded contracts on a notional bond or interest rate, settled daily, used to lock in rates or protect bond values.

points.label: Interest rate swaps
points.description: Two parties exchange interest payments on a notional principal, commonly fixed for floating, letting a borrower change the nature of its debt without refinancing.

points.label: Caps, floors and collars
points.description: A cap limits the maximum rate a borrower pays, a floor sets a minimum rate for a lender, and a collar combines a bought cap and sold floor to reduce the premium.

points.label: Swaptions and choice of instrument
points.description: A swaption gives the right to enter into a swap at a future date; the choice depends on cost, flexibility, counterparty risk and whether the firm wants to keep upside.
points.basis: Derivatives principle: options on swaps and instrument selection
